paper.title: Latent Contextual Bandits and their Application to Personalized Recommendations for New Users

settings.name_in_paper: Latent contextual bandits (sequence of users, each in one of N latent linear classes)
unmapped: Sequence of users (tasks), each user u interacts for T_u <= L steps; each user belongs to one of N unknown latent classes with parameter beta_h; regret summed over all users against each user's true policy
Learner knows the number of latent classes N and the bound L on per-user interactions (used to set J)
Context generation process not specified; Spectral Experts analysis requires i.i.d. samples obtained by uniform random arm selection
Noise variance depends on the latent class
settings.definition_quote: Each user $u$ belongs to one of a finite set of $N$ latent classes... The reward of an arm $a \in \mathcal{A}_{t_u}$ is given by $r_{t_u, a} = \beta_{c_u}^\top x_{t_u, a} + \epsilon_{c_u}$ where $\epsilon_{c_u}$ follows a Gaussian distribution with zero mean and bounded variance.

algorithms.name: LCB with EXP4.P (Latent Contextual Bandits, Spectral Experts + EXP4.P over learned policies)
LCB with EXP3 over learned policies

symbols.L_max: upper bound on per-user interactions T_u
symbols.T_u: number of interactions of user u

conditions: realizability: each user belongs to one of N latent linear models
tuning: separate LinUCB per user in phase 1
Spectral Experts used on i.i.d. uniform samples

source.quote: Set $\tau_u = \sqrt{T_u}$ for all $u \in [\tilde{U}]$ and $J=\sqrt{L}$. Assume $\mathcal{P}$ constructs deterministic policies. If $\mathcal{B}$ is a contextual bandits algorithm with optimal regret bound (e.g.\ EXP4.P), then the problem-independent expected regret bound of LCB with respect to the true policy is ... = O(\sqrt{JS} + d\sqrt{JS\ln (1+S)}) + O(3\sqrt{UT} + \sqrt{UTK\ln N})

results.notes: Regret defined via expected rewards beta^T x against per-user true policy, so pseudo-regret. Proof is heuristic (relies on Spectral Experts O(1/sqrt n) rate). Paper's S and T are phase-1 and phase-2 interaction totals, renamed.

bound.regime: UT >> max{1, d^2/K} JS (T and U grow large)

conditions: realizability: each user belongs to one of N latent linear models

source.quote: ... = O\left(\sqrt{UTK\ln N} \right) as $UT \gg \max\left\{1, \frac{d^2}{K}\right\}JS$, that is, as $T$ and $U$ grows large.

bound.regime: UT >> max{1, d^2/N} JS (T and U grow large)

conditions: realizability: each user belongs to one of N latent linear models
tuning: B = EXP3 treating each learned policy as an arm

source.quote: Similarly, if $\mathcal{B}$ is EXP3~\cite{auer2002nonstochastic} which treats each learned policy as an arm, then the problem-independent expected regret bound of LCB with respect to the true policy is ... = O\left(\sqrt{UTN\ln N} \right) as $UT \gg \max\left\{1, \frac{d^2}{N}\right\}JS$

results.notes: Proof gives phase-2 regret O(3 sqrt(UT) + sqrt(UTN ln N)).

symbols.L_max: upper bound on per-user interactions T_u
symbols.Delta_sep: minimum Euclidean distance between any two latent parameter vectors

conditions: realizability: each user belongs to one of N latent linear models

source.quote: Set $\tau_u = 3$ for all $u \in [\tilde{U}]$ and $J=L^2$. Assume $\mathcal{P}$ constructs deterministic policies and $\mathcal{B}$ is Epoch-Greedy, then the problem-dependent expected regret bound of LCB with respect to the true policy is O(3L^2+dL\sqrt{S\ln(L+1)} + \frac{UK}{\bigtriangleup^2} (\ln N + \ln (T+1)))

results.notes: Delta here is a separation between latent models, not an arm gap; Epoch-Greedy's problem-dependent bound is used with this quantity loosely. Horizon labelled anytime is uncertain; requires L known.
